newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-UniChem sees Lloyds decision soon.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-UniChem sees Lloyds decision soon.

text.p: British pharmaceuticals wholesaler and retailer UniChem Plc said on Tuesday that shareholders at bid target Lloyds Chemists Plc would probably not take too long to decide between its cash-and-share bid and the cash offer from bitter rival German bidder Gehe AG.

"I don't think Lloyds shareholders are going to take a terribly long period to make up their mind, they have had nearly the best part of a year in which to consider these proposals," Jeffery Harris, chief executive at UniChem told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He said UniChem's offer documents would likely be posted to shareholders by the end of this week or early next.
The often verbal battle between UniChem and Gehe reached new heights on Tuesday when the German group launched a fresh cash bid for Lloyds, valuing the company at 650.6 million pounds.
Lloyds responded to the latest Gehe bid by advising its own shareholders to take no action.
UniChem has been locked in a takeover battle for Lloyds with Gehe, a German pharmaceutical wholesaler, since launching a bid for the British drugs chain in February.

"The shadow boxing period is over. I am confident that when it comes to the line that Lloyds' investors will be interested in taking a stake in an integrated business like ours in the healthcare sector," Harris told Reuters.

A fresh offer by UniChem made in October, after the initial one lapsed in March after being referred to Britain's Monopolies and Mergers Commission, is idential to the first and values Lloyds at 657.6 million. It is offering 16 new Unichem shares and 926p in cash for every 10 Lloyds shares.
UniChem, which already owns 9.9 percent of Lloyds, said it believed Gehe could obtain less value from Lloyds Chemists in on-going cost savings and revenue benefits than UniChem.
Gehe, Europe's largest drug distributor, is now offering 500 pence in cash for each share in Lloyds and 322.6p in cash for each Lloyds preference share.
Dieter Kammerer, chairman of Gehe, said in a statement on Tuesday, "This is a highly attractive offer because unlike Unichem's bid it is all cash and is therefore risk-free for Lloyds' shareholders."

Harris responded to Kammerer's comments by telling Reuters, "I think there is an appetite for shares rather than cash in the London market generally at the moment. So I don't believe that is going to be a factor that weighs in their (Gehe) favour. Quite the contrary."

"I don't think his (Kammerer) management team is as good as ours and that is the reason he has underperformed us in the wholesaling business, in terms of operating margins, ever since I have been in this business," added Harris.
UniChem said that despite the public questioning by Gehe of the value of Lloyds, it has taken a consistent view that the underlying value of Lloyds remains unchanged.

"We still believe that Lloyds is as valuable today as it was when we first bid. Essentially the pharmaceutical licenses, and that is what this deal is all about...920 pharmacy licenses, are just as valuable today as they ever were," said Harris.
